findings.issue: Source: 'you shall not scale our walls through any flinching upon my part' (Hector will not flinch, so Diomedes will not get over the wall); candidate: 'You will never climb our walls because I flinched', which says the opposite. Also 'your place at table, the meals they give you' became 'the best seat at table, with generous meals', adding 'best' and 'generous'.
findings.fix: With these words he turned the horses back through the thick of the battle. With a cry that tore the air, the Trojans and Hector showered their missiles after them. Hector shouted to Diomedes, “Son of Tydeus, until now the Danaans have honored you with a place at table, with meals, and with cups filled with wine. From now on they will despise you, because you have become no better than a woman. Get out, you girl and coward! You will never climb our walls through any flinching on my part, and you will never carry off our wives in your ships. I will kill you with my own hand.”

findings.issue: Source 'may earth then swallow me'; candidate 'may the earth swallow me before then' shifts the timing slightly but is a sensible reading.
Source 'Minerva and Juno sat alone, apart from Jove'; candidate keeps 'apart from Zeus' but drops 'alone'.
Simile opener 'As when the stars shine clear' became 'Think of a night when the stars shine clear', a small added address to the reader; both halves of the simile survive.
Source 'honey-sweet corn' rendered 'honey-sweet grain' here, but 'corn' is kept elsewhere (p40, p41); minor inconsistency.
